previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with chest pain and exertional dyspnea, six weeks after a prior cardiac catheterization with stent placement. He reported worsening shortness of breath and recurrent chest pain, prompting evaluation. Initial workup showed no rise in cardiac enzymes, ruling out acute myocardial infarction, but unstable angina was diagnosed. He underwent cardiac catheterization, which revealed new blockages, leading to percutaneous coronary intervention with angioplasty and placement of two stents—one drug-eluting—in the RI and OM1 arteries. He remained hemodynamically stable throughout, with no complications. Metformin was held during admission due to contrast exposure and was to be restarted in two days. He was discharged home in stable condition on dual antiplatelet therapy and optimized medical management for coronary disease, diabetes, hypertension, and hypothyroidism.
